title: Fight phase
subtitle: Build a readable fight phase with a reachable response and a useful recovery.
overview: A health, time, or objective threshold changes the encounter’s rules, moves, arena, or goals to create a distinct stage of the same fight.
learning: Tune the signal, commitment, geometry, response, and recovery of a fight phase as one rule.

demo.title: Test the fight phase
phaseDescriptions: Mark the transition with a pause, animation, music change, camera beat, or environment shift that clearly separates old and new rules.
Give the player a moment to read the new state, reposition, or change priorities before the first unfamiliar threat fully resolves.
The transition ends only after the new arena, objective, and boss state are stable, with a short onboarding beat before the next full-pressure action.

steps.title: Can the player read the complete rule?
steps.body: Mark the transition with a pause, animation, music change, camera beat, or environment shift that clearly separates old and new rules.

steps.title: Is the intended response reachable?
steps.body: Give the player a moment to read the new state, reposition, or change priorities before the first unfamiliar threat fully resolves.

steps.title: Does recovery create a useful outcome?
steps.body: The transition ends only after the new arena, objective, and boss state are stable, with a short onboarding beat before the next full-pressure action.

mistakes.title: Changing several rules during an unprotected attack can make the first failure feel like missing information rather than a design challenge
mistakes.body: Changing several rules during an unprotected attack can make the first failure feel like missing information rather than a design challenge.

mistakes.title: The cue and active geometry disagree
mistakes.body: If the visible fight phase cue promises a different area or timing, the player cannot carry the learned rule into the next cycle.

designNotes.title: Tune the complete rule
designNotes.body: Balance phase length, transition safety, retained hazards, resource state, checkpoints, and how quickly the new rule is introduced.

designNotes.title: Escalate one variable at a time
designNotes.body: Recombine mastered mechanics or change the immediate objective in later phases instead of only increasing health and damage.

designNotes.title: Prove the recovery
designNotes.body: The transition ends only after the new arena, objective, and boss state are stable, with a short onboarding beat before the next full-pressure action.

story.title: What the mechanic communicates
story.body: A health, time, or objective threshold changes the encounter’s rules, moves, arena, or goals to create a distinct stage of the same fight. The encounter uses that rule as a short promise: a visible signal, a committed action, and a result the player can verify.

adaptation.title: Adapt it to the player verbs
adaptation.body: Give the player a moment to read the new state, reposition, or change priorities before the first unfamiliar threat fully resolves. Balance phase length, transition safety, retained hazards, resource state, checkpoints, and how quickly the new rule is introduced.

distinction.title: Keep the mechanic distinct
distinction.body: Changing several rules during an unprotected attack can make the first failure feel like missing information rather than a design challenge. Do not hide that distinction behind extra effects or tracking that the announced rule does not contain.

lensNotes.body: The phase boundary changes a rule or objective and communicates that change explicitly.
State changes are shown clearly enough to tell when the objective has advanced.
Preparation, action, and recovery create a legible cycle of pressure and release.
The mechanic earns its place by preparing, combining, or resolving nearby decisions.
